card.name: Verbs in biology and science explanations
card.fires_on: A verb or noun right after a biological or scientific subject, such as genes, cells or light, in plain explanatory text. It marks the point where the sentence says what the thing does or produces.

modes.label: Verb after cells or genes
modes.description: Action verb describing what cells or genes do, such as generate, arise or making.
modes.example: The Stargardt's gene is copied exclusively in the rod-shaped retinal cells that<< generate>> the eye's peripheral and night vision.

modes.description: A word inside a textbook-style description of a process, such as picking up oxygen or light rays changing direction.

modes.label: Purpose phrase after genes
modes.description: The verb after "for" in a statement of what genes or the genome are for.
modes.example: the instructions for<< building>> that life form.
